findings.why: apply_batch rebuilds the file as raw + bytes(new_bytes); if the existing JSONL lacks a trailing newline the first new line fuses onto the last existing line, corrupting the chain. read_lines/verify tolerate a missing newline but this byte-level reconstruction does not, so the corruption surfaces only on a later read.

_LOCK is a threading.Lock (process-local): append and apply_batch are only mutually exclusive within one process. Two concurrent processes each read-modify-write (read_lines -> read_bytes -> os.replace) and one's fsynced committed record is silently discarded from the source-of-truth JSONL; no flock/fcntl/filelock guards the read-modify-write.
